claims.text: PVD deposition of a TiN coating on a titanium alloy surface will significantly increase surface hardness relative to the untreated alloy.
PVD deposition of a TiN coating on a titanium alloy surface will significantly improve wear resistance relative to the untreated alloy.
The PVD treatment will produce a dense TiN layer.
The PVD-produced TiN layer will adhere well to the titanium alloy substrate.
The TiN layer and underlying titanium alloy will form a hard surface composite.
TiN provides a harder surface because of its intrinsic material properties.
The TiN coating acts as a barrier to abrasion and wear.
The abrasion barrier reduces the rate of surface degradation during mechanical contact.
The coating may increase surface hardness by approximately 100–200% relative to the untreated alloy.
The coating will lower wear rate under mechanical testing conditions.
The hardness and wear-resistance improvements should hold during room-temperature, ambient-humidity sliding wear tests such as pin-on-disk testing.
Very high temperatures or corrosive environments may prevent the expected improvements.
Compromised coating adhesion may prevent the expected hardness and wear-resistance improvements.
Actual performance varies with deposition parameters and coating quality.

contradictions.description: The stated scope assumes a uniform, defect-free, adequately adhered coating, but compromised coating integrity is also presented as a result that would falsify the hypothesis. Coating failure violates the stated boundary condition and therefore cannot cleanly test the in-scope hypothesis.
